title: Valorization of black liquor lignin into renewable absorber coatings for thermal performance enhancement of solar dryers
content:
Abstract

Solar drying is a low energy-consuming technology in agricultural processing; however, its application has been limited by the low absorption capacity and thermal destruction of traditional petroleum-based absorbent coatings. This research discusses the heroization of kraft black liquor lignin as a renewable photothermal absorber coating of mixed-mode solar dryers. Lignin was extract of acid precipitation, then formulated into absorber coats, and fully characterized by physicochemical and optical means of FTIR, XRD, SEM, TGA, and UV–VIS–NIR. Lignin-based formulations were found to have much higher hemispherical absorptance, up to 0.94, and a higher photothermal conversion efficiency ηₚₜ ≈0.46 when compared to a commercial black coating. The evaluation of the solar dryer through an experiment showed improvement in total thermal efficiency as the value changed to about 54–56% of the lignin optimization formulations with reference being about 36%. Response Surface Methodology was used to model and optimize the coating formulation parameters, and the obtained model had R 2 = 0.962 and a statistically insignificant lack-of-fit term. These results support the hypothesis of the conversion of black liquor lignin into high-performance absorber coating successfully to increase solar dryer performance and at the same time increase sustainable biorefinery waste valorization.
